record.original_question: Let Omega ⊂ C^n be a smoothly bounded, pseudoconvex domain. Let V ⊆ Omega be a divisor which is bounded away from the Silov boundary in ∂Omega. Prove that there is a bounded holomorphic function on Omega that vanishes on V. (This is known for the polydisc—a result of Rudin.) -S. Krantz, sk @math.wustl.edu

artifact.category_tag: Zero sets of bounded holomorphic functions
artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ be a smoothly bounded, pseudoconvex domain, and let $H^\infty(\Omega)$ denote the algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on $\Omega$. Let $\partial_S\Omega \subset \partial\Omega$ denote the Shilov boundary of $\Omega$ with respect to $H^\infty(\Omega)$ (i.e., the smallest closed subset of $\partial\Omega$ on which every function in $A(\Omega) = H^\infty(\Omega)\cap C(\overline{\Omega})$ attains its supremum). Let $V \subseteq \Omega$ be a divisor (i.e., the zero set, counted with multiplicities, of a holomorphic function on $\Omega$) such that $V$ is bounded away from $\partial_S\Omega$, in the sense that $\operatorname{dist}(\overline{V}\cap \partial\Omega,\,\partial_S\Omega) > 0$. Prove that there exists a non-trivial bounded holomorphic function $f \in H^\infty(\Omega)$, $f \not\equiv 0$, such that $f$ vanishes on $V$ (with the prescribed multiplicities). (The analogous statement is known for the polydisc, due to Rudin.)
artifact.status_search_result: No direct evidence of a resolution of this problem was found. The problem appears as an open problem posed by S. Krantz, and the closest analogous result is Rudin's theorem for the polydisc. A targeted web search did not return any paper announcing a proof or counterexample for general smoothly bounded pseudoconvex domains; the status therefore remains unverified.
